title: Beacon Ridge Commercial Gas Training Notes: Relief for Small Excursions Above the Band
content:
**The rule.** On Commercial Natural Gas Supply swing excess corrections, small excursions above the band are relieved. The measured excess therms are the cycle usage (the therms on the cycle's energy charge line plus those on its swing excess line) less the upper end of the band, never below zero, and they are compared with the monthly contract volume (the contracted annual therms divided by 12, rounded half up to a whole therm):

| Measured excess therms | Correct excess therms |
|---|---|
| No more than 10 percent (0.10) of the monthly contract volume | Half the measured excess, rounded down to a whole therm |
| Above 10 percent and no more than 20 percent (0.20) of the monthly contract volume | The measured excess multiplied by 0.75, rounded up to a whole therm |
| Above 20 percent of the monthly contract volume | The measured excess, counted as measured |

## Training questions (all figures hypothetical)

**Monthly contract volume 1,250 therms, measured excess 100 therms.** 10 percent of 1,250 is 125. 100 is no more than 125, so the excess is halved: 50 therms.

**Monthly contract volume 1,250 therms, measured excess exactly 125 therms.** 125 is no more than 125, so it is halved: 62.5, rounded down to 62 therms.

**Monthly contract volume 1,000 therms, measured excess 101 therms.** 101 is above 100 (10 percent) and no more than 200 (20 percent). 101 multiplied by 0.75 is 75.75, rounded up to 76 therms.

**Monthly contract volume 1,000 therms, measured excess exactly 200 therms.** 200 is no more than 200, so it is multiplied by 0.75: 150 therms.

**Monthly contract volume 1,000 therms, measured excess 250 therms.** 250 is above 200, so 250 therms are counted as measured.

**Monthly contract volume 1,235 therms, measured excess 123 or 124 therms.** 10 percent of 1,235 is 123.5. 123 is no more than 123.5 and is halved to 61 therms (61.5 rounded down). 124 is above 123.5 and no more than 247, so it becomes 93 therms (124 multiplied by 0.75 is exactly 93).

**Measured excess of 0.** Half of 0 is 0; there are no correct excess therms.
